chapter: Growing up in the Thirteenth Ward
title: The shotgun double and the mixed neighbourhood
summary: He describes the double house, neighbours who came and went, and a mixed Black and white neighbourhood.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: How did you describe it? How did you describe it? Oh the house I grew up in was a shotgun, a double, shotgun double. Oh so you were on one side? Yeah we were on one side and another family on the other side. Yeah. The Day's family. My aunt used to live there first.
Aunt Green, my dad's sister, she lived on the A24 side. Excuse me. Then she left there and I think the Day family. Francois Day and his family, they moved next door.
He had about five or six kids in there.

Then they left and I don't know who else came in after that. Because they had another house in the back. It was like a, a, You had to go through the alley to that place. The Simons lived back there. And several other families had moved in and out through the years. I don't know. Several people moved in. The Payne's, the Hand's family, they moved in there. And they left. And now the Little family, they moved in. And then Susie and Robert Little, they moved in. Then Susie left. Then Robert kept the house about maybe 7, 8, 10 years after she left. Then he left and his son, his name is Robert Jr. He has a house right now. He's renting from me. And I have another lady.
It seems like y'all were the most stable family in the neighborhood.

Yeah, well we stayed there. Yeah, we stayed there. That was a real nice neighborhood. It was a mixed neighborhood. Across the street was the Caucasians. And on this side was the house that I was living in. It was German folks living there. Ms. Selsa and her brother and her mother. And after they all died out, that's when Ms. Richard, who was next door to me, she told me. They didn't ever put a for sale sign on us. But she talked with the lady and we made an offer. And the brothers, they wanted a few dollars more. So we covered the offer. And my wife and I acquired it at 814. Then later on, the house at 822, where we got married at. Well, that went for sale. So we acquired that.
